scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

I'm an 18-year-old guy with a twin sister. My best friend, G, and my sister have had a close relationship since kindergarten. They never officially dated for a long time but were always really into each other. About a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything was great for about 13 months, but then G cheated on my sister. I was the one who found out about it. G begged me not to tell my sister, but I did. I was mad at him, and he was mad at me, so we didn't talk for a month and a half. That was the weirdest time of my life because G is practically like my brother, and not having him around was really hard. After that, G invited me on his family's ski trip as a way to make amends. I went, and in the end, I forgave him and let him back into my life because it was too weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry. He even cried because he felt so bad, and I've only seen him cry once before in my whole life. G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated, and they're still not speaking. My sister is making me feel like shit for still being friends with G. She doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13-year friendship over this. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it. I'll never fully get over it, but I'm not going to let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if my best friend cheated on their SO and felt bad about it, would I end my friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall, a different college in a different state than where my sister is going. So none of this is going to be something we think about when we're living in different places. Am I the asshole? Alright, so I need to figure out if I'm being an asshole here. Let me break it down. First, the betrayal. G cheated on my sister, which is a serious issue. My sister found out, and I was the one who told her. That must have been really hard for her. She's upset with me because I'm still friends with G, and she doesn't understand why I can't just cut ties. On my side, I've known G since kindergarten. We've been inseparable. Losing that friendship would be devastating. I forgave him because I saw his genuine remorse, and I couldn't imagine life without him. Plus, we're going to the same college, so it's practical to maintain the friendship. But my sister feels betrayed, and she's taking it out on me. She's making me feel bad for not cutting ties with G. She doesn't get why I can't just end the friendship, especially since G hurt her. I think about whether I would end a friendship if my best friend cheated on their SO. I probably wouldn't, because the friendship is separate from their personal choices. So why is this different? Because the SO is my sister, it's more personal. But I still see G as my friend, and I can separate his actions from our friendship. Is it wrong to forgive him and keep the friendship? Or is it wrong to not support my sister by cutting ties with G? I also consider the impact on my sister. She's going through a tough time, and I'm her twin, so I should support her. But does that mean I have to end a friendship that's been a huge part of my life? I'm not sure. Maybe I'm being too lenient with G, or maybe my sister is being too harsh. I don't want to lose either of them, but it's causing tension between me and my sister. I think I'm not the asshole because I'm trying to maintain a friendship that's been important to me, and I'm also trying to support my sister, even though she's upset with me. But maybe I'm not considering her feelings enough. Or maybe she's not considering the importance of my friendship with G. I'm confused. I need to figure out if my actions are justified or if I'm being selfish by not cutting ties with G to support my sister.
